# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, 11.3 MB, capture span 2024-07-30 06:38:48 to 06:48:34 UTC+4, ~586 seconds)
- No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory; all attribution below is derived directly from packet content.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Consistent source IP across all suspicious traffic |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | `eth.src` on frames from 172.16.1.66, cross-confirmed by ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4`/`arp.src.hw_mac`) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS name registration (`nbns.name`), DNS self-registration queries, and literally reported inside the malware's own C2 beacon |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos `CNameString` from 172.16.1.66 (AS-REQ/TGS-REQ), and independently reported inside the C2 beacon payload |
| Domain / LAN | wiresharkworkshop.online, 172.16.1.0/24. DC = 172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC), gateway = 172.16.1.1 | DNS SRV lookups, Kerberos, LDAP/CLDAP traffic |
| OS reported by malware | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, Windows Defender only AV | Verbatim field in the C2 beacon string |

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential stealer/downloader).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed via protocol self-identification.** No Suricata/IDS export was provided, but the malware's own C2 "ping" beacon literally contains the string `STRRAT` as a protocol field, alongside a bot ID, hostname, username, OS, and AV status — this is STRRAT's well-documented pipe-delimited check-in format. This is as strong as a signature match, just observed directly in the payload rather than via an IDS rule.

Beacon format observed (TCP stream 83, plaintext, no TLS):
```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active window>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```
The base64 active-window field decoded to `Program Manager`. STRRAT bot ID: `1BE8292C`. Client version reported: `1.6`.

## Behavioral Timeline
1. **T+0s** — normal Windows/AD/Office 365 traffic begins (DHCP-less static host, NBNS, LDAP, Kerberos to the DC, background Microsoft telemetry/CDN traffic — all benign).
2. **T+63.96s** — host resolves `github.com` and `repo1.maven.org` almost simultaneously (1ms apart), consistent with a single local process initiating both lookups.
3. **T+64.05s–64.87s** — small TLS session to `github.com` (140.82.113.3, ~8.5 KB), then a 828 KB download from `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133, GitHub's raw-content CDN).
4. **T+68.01s** — 8.8 MB TLS download from `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, Maven Central's Fastly-fronted CDN).
5. **T+76.99s** — first plaintext TCP SYN from 172.16.1.66:49754 to **141.98.10.79:12132**. STRRAT check-in beacon begins and repeats every ~5 seconds for the remainder of the capture (persistent single session, no TLS).
6. **T+77.87s** — DNS query to `ip-api.com`, followed by an HTTP GET to `ip-api.com/json/` returning victim geolocation (Austin, TX, US) — consistent with malware self-recon/geofencing, occurring within a second of the C2 session starting.

**Delivery chain caveat:** the pcap does not capture a phishing email, lure page, or redirect domain — the visible evidence starts at the near-simultaneous GitHub/Maven Central lookups. Both are legitimate, trusted code-hosting/CDN services; STRRAT campaigns are known to abuse GitHub raw-content links to host jar payloads and to pull a bundled JRE. Because both transfers are TLS-encrypted and no decryption keys are available, the exact request URI, downloaded filename, and file hash cannot be extracted from this capture — only the hosting infrastructure and transfer sizes are observable. These two domains are **not** flagged as malicious IOCs themselves (they are legitimate CDNs), but are noted as probable delivery-stage infrastructure abused to stage the payload.

No other host on the LAN showed beaconing or contacted 141.98.10.79; this is a single-host infection.

## Indicators of Compromise

```json

  "victim": {
    "ip": "172.16.1.66",
    "mac": "00:1e:64:ec:f3:08",
    "hostname": "DESKTOP-SKBR25F",
    "user": "ccollier"
  },
  "malware_family": "STRRAT",
  "attribution_confidence": "signature-confirmed",
  "iocs": [
    {
      "type": "c2_endpoint",
      "value": "141.98.10.79:12132",
      "evidence": "TCP stream 83: persistent plaintext session, 172.16.1.66:49754 <-> 141.98.10.79:12132, ~5s heartbeat interval for full capture duration (T+76.99s to end). Payload contains literal 'ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|...' check-in strings."
    },
    {
      "type": "file_name",
      "value": "STRRAT bot ID 1BE8292C (no on-disk filename observed)",
      "evidence": "Bot identifier field in every C2 beacon message; no cleartext file transfer or filename was observable in the capture (delivery over TLS without keys)."
    }
  ],
  "benign_context": [
    {"host": "github.com (140.82.113.3)", "note": "legitimate GitHub API/web endpoint, small TLS session at T+64.05s, likely staging step prior to payload fetch"},
    {"host": "objects.githubusercontent.com (185.199.110.133)", "note": "legitimate GitHub raw-content CDN, 828 KB TLS download at T+64.83s, probable payload-hosting abuse but content not decryptable from this capture"},
    {"host": "repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209)", "note": "legitimate Maven Central CDN (Fastly), 8.8 MB TLS download at T+68.01s, probable JRE/dependency-hosting abuse, content not decryptable"},
    {"host": "ip-api.com (208.95.112.1)", "note": "legitimate IP geolocation API, queried once at T+77.87s; used here for victim geolocation recon immediately after C2 startup, but the service itself is not malicious infrastructure"},
    {"hosts": "*.msn.com, *.bing.com, *.office.com, *.microsoft.com, *.windows.com, login.microsoftonline.com, javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com, and AD/Kerberos/LDAP/NBNS traffic to 172.16.1.4", "note": "normal Windows 11 / Microsoft 365 / AD-domain background traffic"}
  ],
  "incident_summary": "The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as user ccollier, is infected with the STRRAT Java-based RAT (bot ID 1BE8292C). Roughly one minute into the capture the host fetched files over TLS from GitHub's raw-content CDN and Maven Central (delivery mechanism and exact payload not recoverable from this encrypted traffic), then began a persistent plaintext C2 beacon to 141.98.10.79:12132 every 5 seconds for the rest of the capture, self-identifying via the STRRAT check-in protocol and immediately performing a geolocation lookup via ip-api.com."
}
```

## Recommended Actions
- Isolate 172.16.1.66 from the network immediately.
- Block outbound TCP to 141.98.10.79:12132 at the perimeter firewall.
- Rotate credentials for user `ccollier` (STRRAT is a known credential stealer targeting browsers/email clients).
- Forensically image the host to recover the on-disk STRRAT jar/JRE artifact and compute its SHA256 (not obtainable from this network capture alone).
- Hunt other hosts for the same C2 endpoint and for outbound sessions to `objects.githubusercontent.com` / `repo1.maven.org` in the same time window, in case the delivery chain is shared across multiple victims.
